---
name: docs-update-from-diff
description: Review local code changes with git diff and update the official
  docs under docs/ to match. Use when the user asks to document current
  uncommitted work, sync docs with local changes, update docs after a feature or
  refactor, or when phrases like "git diff", "local changes", "update docs", or
  "official docs" appear.
---

# Docs Update From Diff

## Overview

Inspect local diffs, derive the documentation impact, and update only the
repository's `docs/` pages. Treat the current code as the source of truth and
keep changes scoped, specific, and navigable.

Read [references/docs-surface.md](references/docs-surface.md) before editing if
the affected feature does not map cleanly to an existing docs section.

## Workflow

### 1. Build the change set

Start from local Git state, not from assumptions.

- Inspect `git status --short`, `git diff --stat`, and targeted `git diff`
  output.
- Focus on non-doc changes first so the documentation delta is grounded in
  code.
- Ignore `README.md` and other non-`docs/` content unless they help confirm
  intent.

### 2. Derive the docs impact

For every changed behavior, extract the user-facing or developer-facing facts
that documentation must reflect.

- New command, flag, config key, default, workflow, or limitation
- Renamed behavior or removed behavior
- Changed examples, paths, or setup steps
- New feature that belongs in an existing page but is not mentioned yet

Prefer updating an existing page over creating a new page. Create a new page
only when the feature introduces a stable topic that would make an existing page
harder to follow.

### 3. Find the right docs location

Map each change to the smallest correct documentation surface:

- End-user behavior: `docs/users/**`
- Developer internals, SDKs, contributor workflow, tooling:
  `docs/developers/**`
- Shared landing or navigation changes: root `docs/**` and `_meta.ts`

If you add a new page, update the nearest `_meta.ts` in the same docs section so
the page is discoverable.

### 4. Write the update

Edit documentation with the following bar:

- State the current behavior, not the implementation history
- Use concrete commands, file paths, setting keys, and defaults from the diff
- Remove or rewrite stale text instead of stacking caveats on top of it
- Keep examples aligned with the current CLI and repository layout
- Preserve the repository's existing docs tone and heading structure

### 5. Cross-check before finishing

Verify that the updated docs cover the actual delta:

- Search `docs/` for old names, removed flags, or outdated examples
- Confirm links and relative paths still make sense
- Confirm any new page is included in the relevant `_meta.ts`
- Re-read the changed docs against the code diff, not against memory
- If the diff added, moved, renamed, or removed a page under `docs/users/`,
  verify the `qc-helper` bundled skill's topic-to-path index tables
  (`packages/core/src/skills/bundled/qc-helper/SKILL.md`) are updated to
  match. This skill ships with the CLI and uses hardcoded doc-path tables at
  runtime — stale entries cause `/qc-helper` to miss the right documentation.
  Also check project-level skills under `.qwen/skills/` for hardcoded
  `docs/users/` references that may need updating.

## Practical heuristics

- If a change affects commands, also check quickstart, workflows, and feature
  pages for drift.
- If a change affects configuration, also check
  `docs/users/configuration/settings.md`, feature pages, and auth/provider docs.
- If a change affects tools or agent behavior, check both
  `docs/users/features/**` and `docs/developers/tools/**` when relevant.
- If tests reveal expected behavior more clearly than implementation code, use
  tests to confirm wording.
- If the change adds, moves, renames, or removes a docs page, also update
  hardcoded doc-path consumers: `qc-helper`'s SKILL.md index tables,
  `_meta.ts` navigation files, and any project-level skills under
  `.qwen/skills/` that reference `docs/users/` paths.

## Deliverable

Produce the docs edits under `docs/` that make the current local changes
understandable to a reader who has not seen the diff. Keep the final summary
short and identify which pages were updated.

# Aone Code paths

_Reference file of the `review` skill, loaded on demand — the core body is
already in your context. Read this file BEFORE `match-remote` or `fetch-pr`
when the target is an Aone Code review: a `…/codereview/<id>` URL, a
`pr-url` whose verdict `host` is `code.alibaba-inc.com` or
`gitlab.alibaba-inc.com`, or a bare PR number where `review meta` reports
`platform: "aone"`. GitHub runs never read it._

**`match-remote` on an Aone nested-group target** (`…/<group>/<subgroup…>/<project>/codereview/<id>`): also pass `--group-path <group>/<subgroup…>/<project>` (the URL's full path before `/codereview/`) — owner/repo collapse to the last two segments, and without the full path the matcher could pick a different group's same-named repo.

For an **Aone Code** target, run `/review` **from inside a clone of that repo** (origin on `gitlab.alibaba-inc.com`). The platform is detected from the clone's remote — the read subcommands (`meta`, `fetch-pr`, `issue-context`, `fetch-diff`, `pr-context`, `comment-body` — the fetch the truncation notes pr-context emits name — `test-plan`, which reads the MR description through the same reader, `comment-status`, `presubmit`) work unchanged, backed by the `a1` CLI instead of `gh`, and `--comment` posts through the a1-backed `submit`. (`comment-status` and `presubmit` ARE a1-backed — presubmit fully: self-PR detection, head drift, merge-gate CI, and existing-comment dedup.) The provider refuses an `a1` older than `0.1.90` at authentication time with an upgrade message — that floor is the version the a1-backed flows were probed against. The target number is the global MR id. `fetch-pr` fetches `refs/merge-requests/<id>/head` and builds the worktree + diff as usual, so agents still review the worktree. A `…/codereview/<id>` URL pasted from OUTSIDE a clone of that repo cannot be resolved — the URL's host does pin detection (passed as `--host`), but there is then no clone to fetch the MR ref into and build the worktree/diff from — stop and tell the user to run inside the clone. Pass `--host gitlab.alibaba-inc.com` on the subcommands for Aone targets: it is harmless for the a1-backed commands and makes detection fire regardless of cwd. Aone is one platform under TWO host names — the CR URL carries the web host (`code.alibaba-inc.com`), the clone's remote the git host (`gitlab.alibaba-inc.com`) — and `submit` treats them as one, so passing either to `--host` authorises the post; do not hand-"correct" one into the other.

`pr-context` is Aone-backed — it runs like GitHub (same failure handling: warn, continue, **context-unavailable** state on failure) and reads the MR's metadata, discussion threads, and posted qwen summaries (the machine ledger recovers from them the same way GitHub's does from review bodies). Aone reports no diff stats, so the context file's Diff line degrades — that is expected, not an error. A few flows still must be skipped rather than allowed to hit github.com's same-named repo:

- Agent 0 (issue fidelity) — and, at high or unrecorded effort, the counter-frame audit 6d — run whenever the plan carries the MR identity, as on GitHub: a failed `pr-context` puts the run in the context-unavailable state and both still launch, for their documented unperformable returns (SKILL.md, Step 1). (`issue-context` is a1-backed too, and the fetch Agent 0's brief welds runs it for the MR's workitem evidence exactly as on GitHub.)
- Step 9's bypass audit is platform-aware: on an Aone target it lists the MR's comments through the `a1` CLI and flags any comment the authenticated account posted — or edited — inside the window that `submit`'s receipt does not vouch for. It never queries GitHub for an Aone report.
- `--comment` posts through `qwen review submit` exactly as on GitHub — it routes the write at the `a1` CLI itself (one comment per inline finding, then the summary comment). Aone has **no native request-changes state**: on that verdict the summary comment carries a blocking header, and any inline Criticals block the merge while their discussions stay unresolved — but they carry NO AI-comment flag (`a1` cannot set one), so the platform's dedicated `ai_comment` merge gate does not track them and the discussion gate is the only mechanical block. Relay the `Note:` line `submit` prints about this (it names whether inline Criticals actually posted — and, when they did, which gate they join). The native `a1 repo mr approve` fires for an APPROVE verdict exactly when the run read the MR's context (the same gate as GitHub; a context-unavailable run stays capped at COMMENT). Five failure/refusal shapes are Aone-specific: a **head-drift** refusal (the MR was amended between review and post — re-review the new head, do not re-submit the stale payload, but ONLY while the per-review head-movement restart bound is unspent; once spent, Aone has no submit-at-reviewed-SHA fallback (a1 comments carry no commit anchor), so report that the review cannot be posted against the moved head, leave the findings in the terminal output and the saved report, and leave further re-review/posting to the user); a **mid-batch failure** (stdout carries `"partial": true` with the landed counts/ids and an `ambiguous` flag — part of the review IS on the MR; never re-run `submit`; report what landed and what remains, and leave posting the remainder to the user; when `ambiguous` is true, the FAILED write itself may have reached the MR — a zero count is not proof nothing landed, so tell the user to inspect the MR before hand-posting anything); an **oversized-comment** refusal (a single comment or the summary exceeds a1's 131072-byte single-argument limit — the whole batch refuses before anything lands, there is nothing to re-run, and the user can post by hand); an **ordinary pre-write error** (auth expiry, a network blip — nothing landed, it surfaces as a normal command failure, and a re-run is safe); and the **anchor check** — Aone Code performs NO server-side anchor validation and cannot anchor the old side at all (a `--line` number that names a removed line posts silently on the same-numbered NEW-side line), so `submit` itself validates every inline anchor against the review's captured diff before anything posts: when that diff is not on disk it refuses the whole post (re-run the review so the diff is captured — nothing was written; a `--dry-run` preview is the exception — it writes nothing, so it skips the gate, discloses that anchors went unchecked, and reports `wouldPost: false` with `reason: 'aone-diff-missing'`), and any comment whose anchor it cannot vouch for degrades exactly like GitHub's 422 recovery — a Critical is relocated into the summary body, a Suggestion is discarded and counted — with each one named in the terminal (`Aone anchor check: …`); relay the disclosure. This is also the anchoring PROMISE for an Aone target: new-side only, and a finding on a removed line reaches the MR through the summary body or not at all — never on a wrong line. `submit` also discloses a head that moved DURING posting (`WARNING: the MR head MOVED during posting`) — relay it, and when the post-batch head re-read itself fails, `could not verify` is not `verified stable`: `submit` prints `WARNING: could not re-verify the MR head after posting` (a mid-batch failure prints the same warning naming the failed post) — relay that too. On a second-or-later Aone round, `presubmit`'s overlap dedup applies exactly as on GitHub — a finding already on the MR at the same `(path, line)` is dropped and logged, and only genuinely new findings post; self-PR detection works too (the MR author is matched against `a1 auth whoami`). Two Aone shape notes for that dedup: a1 comments carry no commit anchor, so every `comment-status` thread's code facts (`changedSinceComment`, `touchedBy`) read `unknown`, and a thread the platform marks `outdated` (its line no longer maps after an amend) buckets as stale — so a new finding at a rewritten line still posts — while a resolved (`closed`) thread buckets as `resolved`, exactly like a replied-to thread on GitHub. `publish-assets` stays skipped: the Contents-API write is not Aone-backed.

# Website debugging

Use `bsk_inspect` with `action: "debug"` to record and investigate a website
problem. Keep ordinary browsing capture-free. All examples use the owning
`session`; use returned IDs and the owned `tabId` when targeting a specific tab.
Read loaded schemas for parameters; `debugAction: "capabilities"` reports supported
actions, limits, filters and build information.

## Capture, reproduce, inspect, save

1. Record the problem and expected result. Start a session or borrow the user's tab
   following [tabs and profiles](tabs-and-profiles.md). Start capture **before**
   navigating or reproducing; earlier traffic cannot be recovered.

   ```text
   bsk_inspect({ action: "debug", debugAction: "start", session: "<id>", name: "Nickname does not persist" })
   bsk_page({ action: "navigate", session: "<id>", url: "https://example.com/profile" })
   bsk_inspect({ action: "observe", session: "<id>" })
   ```

2. Retain the returned run ID; pass it as `runId` for subsequent reads. Reproduce
   with ordinary interaction tools, or let the user act (manual capture covers the
   main frame). Observe the outcome; allow expected delayed work to finish.
3. Read `operations`, then `operation` with its `id` to inspect associated requests,
   console messages, field values and later page changes. Use `requests`, then
   `request` with its `id` and `part: "request"` or `"response"` for body text;
   metadata is the default. `console` and `pages` expose other retained context.
4. Use `stop` to save the final record, then export before stopping the session:

   ```text
   bsk_inspect({ action: "debug", debugAction: "stop", session: "<id>" })
   bsk_inspect({ action: "debug", debugAction: "export", session: "<id>", runId: "<run-id>", output: "<new-file.json>" })
   bsk_session({ action: "stop", session: "<id>" })
   ```

`export` writes a new file without overwriting and returns its path/size. Exporting
while capturing gives a point-in-time record. Browser-local history survives task
completion within retention limits; inspect/export it through the extension after
session teardown. A new session cannot read another task's history. Give exported
JSON to an agent for analysis/comparison; there is no repair or comparison action.
`pin`/`unpin` with a completed request `id` protect it from capacity eviction,
not record expiry.

## Decide whether the evidence supports a conclusion

Operation links are time associations, not proof of causation. Distinguish original,
submitted, response and later page values only where recorded; do not invent missing
steps. HTTP 200 is not business success. Console source labels distinguish website,
extension, browser and unknown errors.
`payload_partial` means a field scan was incomplete; inspect the body directly
rather than assuming a unique field match.

Check `run.coverage`, `run.storage`, body states/reasons and `output.omitted`.
Late start, unsupported capture, pending work, truncation, eviction and storage
failure can leave gaps: missing evidence does not mean an event did not happen.
State the supported finding and the specific gap preventing a stronger conclusion.
Evidence may be redacted; never treat displayable text as an exact original request.

## Read within a budget; wait without repeating commands

Default output budget is 64 KiB; `budget` accepts 4096..262144 bytes, export exempt.
For `requests`, filter with `url`, `method`, `resourceType`, `status`, `state` or
`kind`; `kind: "business"` reduces resource noise. Use a comma-separated `fields`
string from capabilities for optional projections. `limit` is 1..100. Requests/operations return `next_since`:
pass it as `since` and merge updates by ID. Body slices return the body's
`next_offset`; console/pages, performance and analysis return top-level `next_offset`. Pass it
as `offset`. Body reads also accept `maxChars` and a JSON `pointer` for complete bodies.
Pagination does not imply completeness: inspect omissions and availability flags.

When busy, read `activity`; use `wait` with `commandId` from activity or
`session_busy`, and optional `waitMs` up to 60000. Omitting `commandId` waits for
idle. Waiting neither resends nor cancels a command; completion is not success.
Inspect the result/page before retrying an operation with uncertain effects.

## Performance and request summaries

`performance` reports main-frame navigation/paint, CLS and long tasks, not INP or
CPU profiles. Read each metric's state/reason and visibility history; hidden-page
or late-start metrics may be invalid.
`aggregate` groups method/path with latency percentiles, errors and slow counts
(`slowMs`). `duplicates` reports suspected equal URL/body/document bursts
(`windowMs`); valid retries or polling can look repetitive. Both default to business
traffic and exclude rule/replay experiments; `includeControlled: true` includes them.
Follow linked request IDs and coverage gaps. Stop capture for stable summary
pagination, using `offset`/`next_offset`, not `since`.

## Explicit network experiments

Capture alone does not alter traffic. Use rules/replay only within the user's
requested experiment: they can block or change live requests and server data.
They require active capture in the original owning task; history never reactivates controls.

`rule_add` takes a **JSON-string** `rule` containing `match`, `effect` and optional
`times`. Match an absolute URL; `*` matches path/query. Effects are `block`,
`modify` (same-origin URL, method, headers, text body or top-level JSON edits) and
`mock` (status, text body, optional headers/delay). Default: one Fetch/XHR match;
first matching rule wins. `times: 0` lasts until disabled/capture ends. Read `rules`
for IDs, hits and failures; `rule_enable`, `rule_disable`, `rule_remove` take `id`.
Capture end clears execution. Check recorded `intervention`; a mock is not a server
response. Active rules also apply to matching replays.

`replay` takes the source request `id` and a **JSON-string** `replay`, for example
`"{\"key\":\"attempt-1\"}"`; add explicit `url`/`body` replacements when needed.
It sends a new request using current cookies. Source, destination and current page
must share an HTTP(S) origin; redirects, cross-origin and binary/multipart replay
are unsupported. Reuse the **same key** after an uncertain result to avoid sending
again; a new key deliberately creates a new attempt. Inspect the linked request
for outcome; replay does not invoke the original page handler or guarantee UI updates.

Reusing retained values requires `integrity.url: "complete"`, complete request metadata
and `request_body.replay_safe: true`. Body `available` only means displayable.
`integrity.metadata` covers the request; `integrity.response_headers` is independent
and does not restrict replay.
Changed, truncated or unverified URL/body require explicit complete replacements;
old records without these markers do too. Never copy a truncated evidence draft as
its replacement. Replacing URL/body cannot fix incomplete metadata. Replace known
redacted headers with authorized values or remove them with `null`; never send
redacted placeholders or guess secrets. Preserve exact numeric tokens when supplying
text bodies; JSON edits must not round large numeric IDs.

---
name: "imagegen"
description: "Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas."
---

# Image Generation Skill

Generates or edits images for the current project (for example website assets, game assets, UI mockups, product mockups, wireframes, logo design, photorealistic images, or infographics).

## Top-level modes and rules

This skill has exactly two top-level modes:

- **Default built-in tool mode (preferred):** built-in `image_gen` tool for image generation, editing, and transparent-image requests. Does not require `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **Fallback CLI mode:** `scripts/image_gen.py` CLI. Use when the user explicitly asks for or confirms the CLI/API/model path. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

Within CLI fallback, the CLI exposes three subcommands:

- `generate`
- `edit`
- `generate-batch`

Rules:
- Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default for normal image generation and editing requests.
- Do not switch to CLI fallback for ordinary quality, size, or file-path control.
- For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha.
- Never silently switch from built-in `image_gen` or CLI `gpt-image-2` to CLI `gpt-image-1.5`; ask the user first unless they explicitly requested `gpt-image-1.5`.
- The word `batch` by itself does not mean CLI fallback. If the user asks for many assets or says to batch-generate assets without explicitly asking for CLI/API/model controls, stay on the built-in path and issue one built-in call per requested asset or variant.
- If the built-in tool fails or is unavailable, tell the user the CLI fallback exists and that it requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Proceed only if the user explicitly asks for that fallback.
- If the user explicitly asks for CLI mode, use the bundled `scripts/image_gen.py` workflow. Do not create one-off SDK runners.
- Never modify `scripts/image_gen.py`. If something is missing, ask the user before doing anything else.

Built-in save-path policy:
- In built-in tool mode, Codex saves generated images under `$CODEX_HOME/*` by default.
- Do not describe or rely on OS temp as the default built-in destination.
- Do not describe or rely on a destination-path argument (if any) on the built-in `image_gen` tool. If a specific location is needed, generate first and then move or copy the selected output from `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...`.
- Save-path precedence in built-in mode:
  1. If the user names a destination, move or copy the selected output there.
  2. If the image is meant for the current project, move or copy the final selected image into the workspace before finishing.
  3. If the image is only for preview or brainstorming, render it inline; the underlying file can remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
- Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
- Do not overwrite an existing asset unless the user explicitly asked for replacement; otherwise create a sibling versioned filename such as `hero-v2.png` or `item-icon-edited.png`.

Shared prompt guidance for both modes lives in `references/prompting.md` and `references/sample-prompts.md`.

Fallback-only docs/resources for CLI mode:
- `references/cli.md`
- `references/image-api.md`
- `references/codex-network.md`
- `scripts/image_gen.py`

## When to use
- Generate a new image (concept art, product shot, cover, website hero)
- Generate a new image using one or more reference images for style, composition, or mood
- Edit an existing image (inpainting, lighting or weather transformations, background replacement, object removal, compositing, transparent background)
- Produce many assets or variants for one task

## When not to use
- Extending or matching an existing SVG/vector icon set, logo system, or illustration library inside the repo
- Creating simple shapes, diagrams, wireframes, or icons that are better produced directly in SVG, HTML/CSS, or canvas
- Making a small project-local asset edit when the source file already exists in an editable native format
- Any task where the user clearly wants deterministic code-native output instead of a generated bitmap

## Decision tree

Think about two separate questions:

1. **Intent:** is this a new image or an edit of an existing image?
2. **Execution strategy:** is this one asset or many assets/variants?

Intent:
- If the user wants to modify an existing image while preserving parts of it, treat the request as **edit**.
- If the user provides images only as references for style, composition, mood, or subject guidance, treat the request as **generate**.
- If the user provides no images, treat the request as **generate**.

Built-in edit semantics:
- Built-in edit mode is for images already visible in the conversation context, such as attached images or images generated earlier in the thread.
- If the user wants to edit a local image file with the built-in tool, first load it with built-in `view_image` tool so the image is visible in the conversation context, then proceed with the built-in edit flow.
- Do not promise arbitrary filesystem-path editing through the built-in tool.
- If a local file still needs direct file-path control, masks, or other explicit CLI-only parameters, use the explicit CLI fallback only when the user asks for it.
- For edits, preserve invariants aggressively and save non-destructively by default.

Execution strategy:
- In the built-in default path, produce many assets or variants by issuing one `image_gen` call per requested asset or variant.
- In the CLI fallback path, use the CLI `generate-batch` subcommand only when the user explicitly chose CLI mode and needs many prompts/assets.
- For many distinct assets, do not use `n` as a substitute for separate prompts. `n` is for variants of one prompt; distinct assets need distinct built-in calls or distinct CLI `generate-batch` jobs.

Assume the user wants a new image unless they clearly ask to change an existing one.

## Workflow
1. Decide the top-level mode: built-in by default, including transparent-output requests; fallback CLI only if explicitly requested or confirmed.
2. Decide the intent: `generate` or `edit`.
3. Decide whether the output is preview-only or meant to be consumed by the current project.
4. Decide the execution strategy: single asset vs repeated built-in calls vs CLI `generate-batch`.
5. Collect inputs up front: prompt(s), exact text (verbatim), constraints/avoid list, and any input images.
6. For every input image, label its role explicitly:
   - reference image
   - edit target
   - supporting insert/style/compositing input
7. If the edit target is only on the local filesystem and you are staying on the built-in path, inspect it with `view_image` first so the image is available in conversation context.
8. If the user asked for a photo, illustration, sprite, product image, banner, or other explicitly raster-style asset, use `image_gen` rather than substituting SVG/HTML/CSS placeholders. If the request is for an icon, logo, or UI graphic that should match existing repo-native SVG/vector/code assets, prefer editing those directly instead.
9. Augment the prompt based on specificity:
   - If the user's prompt is already specific and detailed, normalize it into a clear spec without adding creative requirements.
   - If the user's prompt is generic, add tasteful augmentation only when it materially improves output quality.
10. Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default.
11. For transparent-output requests, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha channel.
12. Inspect outputs and validate: subject, style, composition, text accuracy, and invariants/avoid items.
13. Iterate with a single targeted change, then re-check.
14. For preview-only work, render the image inline; the underlying file may remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
15. For project-bound work, move or copy the selected artifact into the workspace and update any consuming code or references. Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
16. For batches or multi-asset requests, persist every requested deliverable final in the workspace unless the user explicitly asked to keep outputs preview-only. Discarded variants do not need to be kept unless requested.
17. If the user explicitly chooses or confirms the CLI fallback, then use the fallback-only docs for model, quality, size, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, output paths, and network setup.
18. Always report the final saved path(s) for any workspace-bound asset(s), plus the final prompt or prompt set and whether the built-in tool or fallback CLI mode was used.

## Transparent image requests

Ask built-in `image_gen` for a genuinely transparent background and preserve its alpha.

## Prompt augmentation

Reformat user prompts into a structured, production-oriented spec. Make the user's goal clearer and more actionable, but do not blindly add detail.

Treat this as prompt-shaping guidance, not a closed schema. Use only the lines that help, and add a short extra labeled line when it materially improves clarity.

### Specificity policy

Use the user's prompt specificity to decide how much augmentation is appropriate:

- If the prompt is already specific and detailed, preserve that specificity and only normalize/structure it.
- If the prompt is generic, you may add tasteful augmentation when it will materially improve the result.

Allowed augmentations:
- composition or framing hints
- polish level or intended-use hints
- practical layout guidance
- reasonable scene concreteness that supports the stated request

Not allowed augmentations:
- extra characters or objects that are not implied by the request
- brand names, slogans, palettes, or narrative beats that are not implied
- arbitrary side-specific placement unless the surrounding layout supports it

## Use-case taxonomy (exact slugs)

Classify each request into one of these buckets and keep the slug consistent across prompts and references.

Generate:
- photorealistic-natural — candid/editorial lifestyle scenes with real texture and natural lighting.
- product-mockup — product/packaging shots, catalog imagery, merch concepts.
- ui-mockup — app/web interface mockups and wireframes; specify the desired fidelity.
- infographic-diagram — diagrams/infographics with structured layout and text.
- scientific-educational — classroom explainers, scientific diagrams, and learning visuals with required labels and accuracy constraints.
- ads-marketing — campaign concepts and ad creatives with audience, brand position, scene, and exact tagline/copy.
- productivity-visual — slide, chart, workflow, and data-heavy business visuals.
- logo-brand — logo/mark exploration, vector-friendly.
- illustration-story — comics, children’s book art, narrative scenes.
- stylized-concept — style-driven concept art, 3D/stylized renders.
- historical-scene — period-accurate/world-knowledge scenes.

Edit:
- text-localization — translate/replace in-image text, preserve layout.
- identity-preserve — try-on, person-in-scene; lock face/body/pose.
- precise-object-edit — remove/replace a specific element (including interior swaps).
- lighting-weather — time-of-day/season/atmosphere changes only.
- background-extraction — transparent background / clean cutout. Ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency.
- style-transfer — apply reference style while changing subject/scene.
- compositing — multi-image insert/merge with matched lighting/perspective.
- sketch-to-render — drawing/line art to photoreal render.

## Shared prompt schema

Use the following labeled spec as shared prompt scaffolding for both top-level modes:

```text
Use case: <taxonomy slug>
Asset type: <where the asset will be used>
Primary request: <user's main prompt>
Input images: <Image 1: role; Image 2: role> (optional)
Scene/backdrop: <environment>
Subject: <main subject>
Style/medium: <photo/illustration/3D/etc>
Composition/framing: <wide/close/top-down; placement>
Lighting/mood: <lighting + mood>
Color palette: <palette notes>
Materials/textures: <surface details>
Text (verbatim): "<exact text>"
Constraints: <must keep/must avoid>
Avoid: <negative constraints>
```

Notes:
- `Asset type` and `Input images` are prompt scaffolding, not dedicated CLI flags.
- `Scene/backdrop` refers to the visual setting. It is not the same as the fallback CLI `background` parameter, which controls output transparency behavior.
- Fallback-only execution notes such as `Quality:`, `Input fidelity:`, masks, output format, and output paths belong in the CLI path only. Do not treat them as built-in `image_gen` tool arguments.

Augmentation rules:
- Keep it short.
- Add only the details needed to improve the prompt materially.
- For edits, explicitly list invariants (`change only X; keep Y unchanged`).
- If any critical detail is missing and blocks success, ask a question; otherwise proceed.

## Examples

### Generation example (hero image)
```text
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: landing page hero
Primary request: a minimal hero image of a ceramic coffee mug
Style/medium: clean product photography
Composition/framing: wide composition with usable negative space for page copy if needed
Lighting/mood: soft studio lighting
Constraints: no logos, no text, no watermark
```

### Edit example (invariants)
```text
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: product photo background replacement
Primary request: replace only the background with a warm sunset gradient
Constraints: change only the background; keep the product and its edges unchanged; no text; no watermark
```

## Prompting best practices
- Structure prompt as scene/backdrop -> subject -> details -> constraints.
- Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the mode and polish level.
- Use camera/composition language for photorealism.
- Only use SVG/vector stand-ins when the user explicitly asked for vector output or a non-image placeholder.
- Quote exact text and specify typography + placement.
- For tricky words, spell them letter-by-letter and require verbatim rendering.
- For multi-image inputs, reference images by index and describe how they should be used.
- For edits, repeat invariants every iteration to reduce drift.
- Iterate with single-change follow-ups.
- If the prompt is generic, add only the extra detail that will materially help.
- If the prompt is already detailed, normalize it instead of expanding it.
- For CLI fallback only, see `references/cli.md` and `references/image-api.md` for model, `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output-path guidance.
- For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency and preserve its alpha.

More principles shared by both modes: `references/prompting.md`.
Copy/paste specs shared by both modes: `references/sample-prompts.md`.

## Guidance by asset type
Asset-type templates (website assets, game assets, wireframes, logo) are consolidated in `references/sample-prompts.md`.

## gpt-image-2 guidance for CLI fallback

The fallback CLI defaults to `gpt-image-2`.

- Use `gpt-image-2` for new CLI/API workflows unless the user confirms a different model.
- CLI `gpt-image-2` does not support `background=transparent`; ask before using `gpt-image-1.5` unless the user explicitly requested that model.
- `gpt-image-2` always uses high fidelity for image inputs; do not set `input_fidelity` with this model.
- `gpt-image-2` supports `quality` values `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `auto`.
- Use `quality low` for fast drafts, thumbnails, and quick iterations. Use `medium`, `high`, or `auto` for final assets, dense text, diagrams, identity-sensitive edits, or high-resolution outputs.
- Square images are typically fastest to generate. Use `1024x1024` for fast square drafts.
- If the user asks for 4K-style output, use `3840x2160` for landscape or `2160x3840` for portrait.
- `gpt-image-2` size may be `auto` or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` if all constraints hold: max edge `<= 3840px`, both edges multiples of `16px`, long-to-short ratio `<= 3:1`, total pixels between `655,360` and `8,294,400`.

Popular `gpt-image-2` sizes:
- `1024x1024` square
- `1536x1024` landscape
- `1024x1536` portrait
- `2048x2048` 2K square
- `2048x1152` 2K landscape
- `3840x2160` 4K landscape
- `2160x3840` 4K portrait
- `auto`

## Fallback CLI mode only

### Temp and output conventions
These conventions apply only to the CLI fallback. They do not describe built-in `image_gen` output behavior.
- Use `tmp/imagegen/` for intermediate files (for example JSONL batches); delete them when done.
- Write final artifacts under `output/imagegen/`.
- Use `--out` or `--out-dir` to control output paths; keep filenames stable and descriptive.

### Dependencies
Prefer `uv` for dependency management in this repo.

Required Python package:
```bash
uv pip install openai
```

Optional for image inspection and downscaling:
```bash
uv pip install pillow
```

Portability note:
- If you are using the installed skill outside this repo, install dependencies into that environment with its package manager.
- In uv-managed environments, `uv pip install ...` remains the preferred path.

### Environment
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be set for live API calls.
- Do not ask the user for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when using the built-in `image_gen` tool.
- Never ask the user to paste the full key in chat. Ask them to set it locally and confirm when ready.

If the key is missing, give the user these steps:
1. Create an API key in the OpenAI platform UI: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
2. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` as an environment variable in their system.
3. Offer to guide them through setting the environment variable for their OS/shell if needed.

If installation is not possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it into their active environment.

### Script-mode notes
- CLI commands + examples: `references/cli.md`
- API parameter quick reference: `references/image-api.md`
- Network approvals / sandbox settings for CLI mode: `references/codex-network.md`

## Reference map
- `references/prompting.md`: shared prompting principles for both modes.
- `references/sample-prompts.md`: shared copy/paste prompt recipes for both modes.
- `references/cli.md`: fallback-only CLI usage via `scripts/image_gen.py`.
- `references/image-api.md`: fallback-only API/CLI parameter reference.
- `references/codex-network.md`: fallback-only network/sandbox troubleshooting for CLI mode.
- `scripts/image_gen.py`: fallback-only CLI implementation. Use only when the user explicitly chooses or confirms CLI mode.

# openai.yaml fields (full example + descriptions)

`agents/openai.yaml` is an extended, product-specific config intended for the machine/harness to read, not the agent. Other product-specific config can also live in the `agents/` folder.

## Full example

```yaml
interface:
  display_name: "Optional user-facing name"
  short_description: "Optional user-facing description"
  icon_small: "./assets/small-400px.png"
  icon_large: "./assets/large-logo.svg"
  brand_color: "#3B82F6"
  default_prompt: "Optional surrounding prompt to use the skill with"

dependencies:
  tools:
    - type: "mcp"
      value: "github"
      description: "GitHub MCP server"
      transport: "streamable_http"
      url: "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"

policy:
  allow_implicit_invocation: true
```

## Field descriptions and constraints

Top-level constraints:

- Quote all string values.
- Keep keys unquoted.
- For `interface.default_prompt`: generate a helpful, short (typically 1 sentence) example starting prompt based on the skill. It must explicitly mention the skill as `$skill-name` (e.g., "Use $skill-name-here to draft a concise weekly status update.").

- `interface.display_name`: Human-facing title shown in UI skill lists and chips.
- `interface.short_description`: Human-facing short UI blurb (25–64 chars) for quick scanning.
- `interface.icon_small`: Path to a small icon asset (relative to skill dir). Default to `./assets/` and place icons in the skill's `assets/` folder.
- `interface.icon_large`: Path to a larger logo asset (relative to skill dir). Default to `./assets/` and place icons in the skill's `assets/` folder.
- `interface.brand_color`: Hex color used for UI accents (e.g., badges).
- `interface.default_prompt`: Default prompt snippet inserted when invoking the skill.
- `dependencies.tools[].type`: Dependency category. Only `mcp` is supported for now.
- `dependencies.tools[].value`: Identifier of the tool or dependency.
- `dependencies.tools[].description`: Human-readable explanation of the dependency.
- `dependencies.tools[].transport`: Connection type when `type` is `mcp`.
- `dependencies.tools[].url`: MCP server URL when `type` is `mcp`.
- `policy.allow_implicit_invocation`: When false, the skill is not injected into
  the model context by default, but can still be invoked explicitly via `$skill`.
  Defaults to true.

# 第一阶段深度范例（写正文前读取）

写正文前读取本文。下面是一份**完整的第一阶段范例正文（医药板块）**，用来示范"每个分析点该写到多深"以及当前结构怎么落地。结构与格式以 `chat_contract.md` 为准，本文只多给一件事：**深度**。

使用方法：照着这份范例的**深度**写，不是照搬它的数字或结论（数字为示例）。**本文件的说明性文字（本段、以及范例末尾的"为什么这样算够深"）不要写进给用户的正文。**

判断深度是否达标的统一标尺（每个分析点都要过）：

- 每条"本段结论"含三件：**综合判断 + 关键理由 + 对"能不能追/持续性"的启示**，不是把数字重述一遍。
- 模块1 每格"解读"走"状态 → 市场行为 → 持续性含义"，落到"对结论的权重"。
- 模块2 每条"为什么重要"是一条**传导链（X → Y → Z）**，不是"利好板块/提振情绪"的标签。
- 模块3 每组解释的是**结构含义**（这组为什么重要、对扩散/退潮意味着什么），不是列股票名。
- 模块4 每条信号点名一个**胜负手变量** + 可量化阈值 + 改善/恶化双向。
- 模块5 每条风险有**可观察触发条件** + 出现后主结论如何被推翻。

---

## 范例正文（医药）

回答基于AI 生成，仅用于信息参考与研究辅助，不构成任何投资建议。股市有风险，请结合自身风险承受能力决策。

目标概念板块：医药行业（932132）；数据截至 2026-06-18 收盘；本次以该板块成分中市值最大的 10 只代表股为样本观察短期热度；综合热度 3/5（活跃）。

标题：底部有基础，但反转还没确认

催化质量较高（ASCO、医保预申报、国办 9 号文密集落地），但行情端只有 CRO/CDMO/创新药方向兑现放量上涨、器械与传统中药同日下跌，兑现尚不充分；整体更像"结构性修复"而不是"板块反转"，属"可观察、未到可追"的一类。

收盘点位：9449 点；恒瑞医药（代表股）当日 PE(TTM)：40 倍；近7日涨跌幅：−1.4%；近7个交易日日均成交额：796 亿。
本次选取的 10 只代表股：药明康德、迈瑞医疗、云南白药、联影医疗、爱尔眼科、片仔癀、凯莱英、百奥赛图、康龙化成、华润三九。

## 直接回答

您问的是"医药连跌后放量反弹、热度高涨，是否见底反转"。

**问题**：医药板块放量反弹后能否确认见底反转、当前能不能追。
**结论**：还不能确认见底反转，更准确的定性是"政策 + 产业催化驱动的结构性超跌修复"——6月18日放量 +1.03% 的背后是极端分化（CRO/CDMO 平均涨超 5%、器械龙头平均跌超 4%），资金只在创新药一条线做多，不是底部普涨信号；板块仍在 9352–9544 箱体内，单日放量阳线是箱体内反弹而非突破。
**下一步**：盯量价能否持续接力。改善——连续放量站上 9544，修复升级为底部反转、可逢回调参与；恶化——缩量回落跌破 9352，确认箱体震荡、反弹只是为下一轮卖出提供流动性，应回避。

## 现在有多热

**本段结论：**四维呈"放量 + 低估值支撑"的活跃格局，但扩散面窄、价格未突破前高（9449 < 6月12日高点 9544），最大的撕裂在于催化密度已到高热档、行情只在 CRO/创新药局部兑现——属"活跃但未确认"，趋势确认要靠放量突破而非单日反弹。

| 维度 | 数值 | 状态 | 解读 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 价格涨跌 | 6月18日 +1.03%（收盘 9449）；6月8日以来在 9352–9544 箱体内 | 弱确认 | 当日涨幅是连跌三天后的修复，但收盘仍低于 6月12日高点 9544、未形成更高高点，仍在"跌→弹→再跌→再弹"的箱体里；底部确认需突破 9544 而非仅仅反弹，因此当前价格只支持"超跌修复"、不支持"趋势反转"。 |
| 成交量能 | 6月18日成交 956 亿、量比约 1.35（前日 707 亿，放量约 35%） | 确认 | 当日较前一日放量约 35%、为 6月以来第二大成交，说明有增量资金进场；但 6月12日同样放量反弹后三天回吐，单日放量不足以确认趋势，连续放量才有意义——这是决定本轮性质的最关键待验证变量。 |
| 代表股表现 | 10 只中 4 只上涨（CRO/CDMO/生物技术全线走强）、6 只下跌（器械 + 传统中药走弱） | 弱确认 | 极端分化：上涨的全是创新药外包链、下跌的覆盖器械与传统药，说明资金在做"弃旧换新"的结构性调仓而非底部普涨，指数 +1.03% 掩盖了激烈内部轮动，反弹质量因此打折。 |
| 估值位置 | 10 只代表股 PE(TTM) 中位数约 25x、区间约 12–145x（截至 6月18日） | 确认 | 核心资产估值分化大，部分龙头处历史极低分位、具深度价值属性；低估值给多方"跌不深"的底气、构成安全边际，但能否转化为上涨取决于基本面兑现速度，是必要条件而非充分条件。 |

## 为什么涨 / 跌

**本段结论：**本轮反弹的真正驱动是政策环境从"压制创新"到"扶持创新"的范式转换——主驱动是产业定位升级（国办 9 号文 + 十五五"四大支柱"，确定性最高、影响最持久），次驱动是 ASCO 验证的出海竞争力，反腐则是出清旧营销模式、与扶持真创新并不矛盾；证据链偏强，但行情兑现集中在创新药一条线，能否持续仍取决于扩散。

### 6月18日｜信息来源：证券日报｜生物医药被列为"四大新兴支柱产业"，创新药板块集体启动

**事实**：国家层面首次将生物医药与半导体并列为"四大新兴支柱产业"，多重政策窗口集中兑现。
🔗 **为什么重要**：定位升级到与半导体同等战略高度，意味着后续研发补贴、税收优惠、审批绿色通道有望参照半导体模式加码，从根本上抬高行业估值天花板，而非一次性情绪刺激。
🔍 **后续验证**：盯十五五规划正式稿对生物医药的篇幅与具体扶持措施；若配套力度明显弱于半导体，则其估值含义需下修、本条催化降级。

### 6月8日｜信息来源：央视网｜14 部门联合发文继续整治医药购销，反腐加码

**事实**：14 个部门联合发文，重点打击借学术活动名义非法营销及耗材设备采购违规，同日板块大跌。
🔗 **为什么重要**：反腐是过去两年板块承压的核心因素，学术推广型药企销售费用承压直接冲击收入端；但出清的是旧营销模式、真创新药是政策保护对象——它压制器械/传统药、相对利好创新药，这正是当日极端分化的政策根源。
🔍 **后续验证**：盯执法是否扩大到头部创新药企；若仅集中在低端仿制药与耗材，对核心资产实质冲击有限、分化逻辑延续。

### 5月29日｜信息来源：新华社｜中国创新药企在 ASCO 年会密集披露临床数据

**事实**：多家国产创新药企在 ASCO 年会公布关键临床数据，多项结果获国际同行关注。
🔗 **为什么重要**：ASCO 是全球肿瘤领域最高级别会议，国产数据获认可意味着创新药出海与对外授权（License-out）逻辑获实质验证，直接支撑 CRO/CDMO 这条"卖铲人"链条的景气预期。
🔍 **后续验证**：盯相关品种后续能否落地海外授权或合作订单；若只停在数据披露、无商业化跟进，则产业催化的力度要打折。

## 谁在动、谁没动

**本段结论：**极端的结构性分化而非普涨——资金沿创新药景气度最高的"卖铲人"（CRO/CDMO）精准做多，同时从反腐承压的器械与传统中药调仓换股，本质是"弃旧换新"；这种"龙头单线带队、尚未扩散"的结构意味着反弹质量取决于能否从创新药外溢到全板块，否则又是一次集中脉冲。

- **放量上攻**：药明康德、凯莱英、百奥赛图、康龙化成——全是 CRO/CDMO/生物技术平台（创新药外包与源头研发链），直接受益于 ASCO 验证的全球竞争力、医保预申报缩短商业化周期、国办 9 号文的定价保护，量价齐升说明机构资金坚定看好这一方向，是本轮主线。
- **缩量上行**：无。
- **缩量回调**：云南白药、爱尔眼科、片仔癀、华润三九——传统中药与消费医疗缩量小幅收跌、抛压衰竭但未获增量买盘，不在本轮政策催化核心受益链上，处于"不涨不跌"的中间观察带，是后续能否扩散的风向标。
- **放量杀跌**：迈瑞医疗、联影医疗——器械双龙头在反弹日逆势放量下跌，6月8日文件直指"耗材设备采购违规"形成压制，叠加海外关税扰动，资金在创新药起势时从器械调仓换股；它们是"弃旧换新"被卖出的一端，也是判断反弹能否全面化的反向温度计。

## 接下来盯什么

**本段结论：**当前最悬而未决的是这轮反弹是又一次"拉一根随后继续跌"、还是结构性修复的起点；最快能验证的是量价持续性——连续放量站稳前高即可排除"死猫跳"，反之缩量回落则确认箱体震荡；其次看创新药的强势能否外溢到器械。

📈 **信号1 · 量能**：板块成交能否持续放量、指数能否站上前高。
**盯**：接下来连续 3 个交易日成交维持 900 亿以上且站稳 9544。
**改善**：连续放量突破前高，修复从"超跌反弹"升级为"底部反转"，可逢回调参与。
**恶化**：反弹后缩量回落至 9350 以下，再次确认箱体震荡，每次反弹都是卖点。

📈 **信号2 · 扩散**：器械龙头能否从下跌转为同步跟涨。
**盯**：下一个反弹日迈瑞、联影是否同步收红、上涨家数能否过半。
**改善**：器械跟涨说明资金从"抱团创新药"转向"全板块做多"，底部确认概率大增。
**恶化**：创新药继续独涨、器械继续跌，确认是纯结构轮动而非趋势反转。

📈 **信号3 · 政策**：十五五生物医药扶持措施与创新药定价细则的落地力度。
**盯**：接下来一个季度配套细则是否出台、扶持范围与降幅限制是否超预期。
**改善**：扶持力度超预期（如设立医药产业基金），板块估值中枢系统性上移。
**恶化**：细则范围窄、力度弱，"四大支柱产业"定位的估值含义被证伪。

📈 **信号4 · 外资**：北向资金对医药板块的配置方向。
**盯**：北向对医药的净买入/净卖出方向与规模能否转正并持续。
**改善**：外资持续增配叠加内资共振，趋势反转概率大增。
**恶化**：北向持续卖出，说明地缘风险仍压制外资配置意愿。

## 风险提示

**本段结论：**最该警惕的是"利好兑现后资金出逃"——过去半年医药板块反复上演这一剧本；若当前热度提升只是为下一轮卖出提供流动性，则本次反弹投资价值为负，只有量价持续 + 扩散同时出现才能排除；其次是领涨方向恰是出海最敏感的一批，外部限制属尾部但杀伤大的风险。

⚠️ **风险1 · 利好兑现后资金出逃**
**触发**：政策细则公布当日/次日板块低开放量下跌；"利好出尽是利空"是近半年反复上演的剧本，当前涨的是预期，兑现后预期落地反而成卖点。
**证伪**：若政策公布后连续 3 个交易日放量突破箱体上沿，则该判断失效、修复升级为趋势。

⚠️ **风险2 · 创新药出海受阻**
**触发**：美国对中国生物医药企业加征限制正式落地（如药明系/康龙系被列入受限名单）；本轮领涨方向恰是出海最敏感的一批、海外收入占比高，一旦受限直接打掉景气逻辑。
**证伪**：若出现新增制裁或订单取消率骤升，则修复判断即刻失效、应从进攻转防御。

⚠️ **风险3 · 反弹后再次急杀**
**触发**：连续缩量下跌、跌穿 6月17日低点 9352；板块已形成"反弹—卖出"负反馈，跌破箱体下沿意味着多头防线失守。
**证伪**：若放量站回箱体中枢上方，则负反馈被打破、反弹仍有效。

## 信息来源

- 证券日报：生物医药被列为"四大新兴支柱产业"，2026-06-18，<URL>
- 央视网：14 部门联合发文整治医药购销，2026-06-08，<URL>
- 新华社：中国创新药企 ASCO 年会披露临床数据，2026-05-29，<URL>
- seed_finance_search：板块与 10 股行情、成交、估值及近7个交易日序列。

下一步是否为您生成飞书文档版？如果需要，请回复"生成飞书文档"。

---

## 为什么这样算够深（仅供理解，勿写进正文）

- **直接回答**的"结论"没有停在"偏热/不建议追"，而是给了定性（结构性超跌修复）+ 核心原因（只有创新药一条线放量）；"下一步"把改善与恶化都写成可观察的价格条件。
- **模块1**每格"解读"都落到"对结论的权重"：价格只支持超跌修复、量能点出"连续放量才是胜负手"、代表股点破"反弹质量打折"、估值定性为"必要非充分条件"。
- **模块2**每条"为什么重要"都是传导链（定位升级 → 补贴/绿色通道参照半导体 → 抬高天花板），且本段结论排了主次驱动、给了证据强弱。
- **模块3**两端（放量上攻/放量杀跌）讲清"为什么"与"意味着什么"，把分化升华成"弃旧换新、能否外溢"的结构判断。
- **模块4**每条信号都点名胜负手变量 + 可量化阈值 + 双向解读，且全是未来变量、不含截止日前的具体日历日期。
- **模块5**每条风险有可观察触发 + 出现后主结论如何被推翻，而不是"政策不及预期/情绪转弱"。

# 创作发布工作流（仅“文字配图”发帖：文字做成图片）

目标：在“收集整理”的素材基础上或直接按用户提供内容，完成有原创表达的笔记创作，并在获得用户明确授权且当前环境可操作时，用“文字配图”完成发帖发布。

## 适用范围（不满足则直接中止并告知原因）

- 仅当用户需求表达为：想发一个“文字是图片/大字图/文字配图”的图文笔记时，才执行本工作流
- 若用户提供图片/视频，或要求我搜索下载图片并上传发布：直接停止并回复当前不支持上传图片/视频；可改为“文字配图”或由用户手动上传后我再继续填标题/正文/标签

## 输入信息（缺什么先补什么）

- 主题与目标：想解决谁的什么问题（选购/避坑/路线/清单/体验）
- 受众画像：新手/进阶、预算区间、肤质/场景、城市/出行天数
- 素材来源：来自收集文档、你的浏览记录、你提供的图片/视频、或你提供的链接/截图
- 风格偏好：干货清单 / 体验叙事 / 对比测评 / 省钱攻略
- 发布约束：不能写的点（合规/品牌/敏感词），是否需要“更克制/更夸张”

## 工作流

### 1) 选角度与差异化

- 从素材里挑 3-5 条“高价值点”（方法、坑点、结论、清单、对比维度）
- 定义你的差异化：
  - 更具体：用数字、步骤、条件、场景限定替代空泛形容
  - 更可执行：把经验转成“怎么做/怎么选/怎么安排”
  - 更可信：明确前提与边界（人群/预算/季节/肤质/机型）

### 2) 产出大纲（先结构后文案）

推荐结构（按需选用）：

- 开头：一句话结论 + 适用人群/前提
- 正文：3-6 个小节（对比维度/路线安排/步骤清单/避坑要点）
- 补充：预算/替代方案/注意事项/常见问答
- 收尾：总结 + 行动建议 + 互动引导（评论区提问）

### 3) 改写规则（避免“拼贴感”）

- 不直接复用原笔记的句子与段落，使用自己的表达重写
- 保留事实与逻辑，但重组叙事顺序与表达方式
- 给出你的判断依据与使用前提，避免绝对化、医疗化与夸大承诺
- 引用对标内容时，以“思路/结构/要点”复用为主，不复用原文表达

### 4) 生成可发布内容包（标题/正文/标签严格分离）

至少包含：

- 标题候选 5-10 个（覆盖：结论型/避坑型/清单型/对比型/人群型）
- 正文 1 版主稿 + 1 版更短更利落的备选
- 封面文案建议（3-5 条，控制在短句）
- 标签矩阵（10-20 个：大词 + 场景词 + 人群词 + 城市/机型/肤质等限定词）
- 互动引导（2-3 条）：提问、投票、求建议、想看下一篇

### 5) 文字配图（大字图）生成

约束：当前仅支持在“文字配图”模块生成一张大字图用于发布，不支持上传用户本地图片/视频。

- 生成 1 张大字图方案：
  - 大字文案（10-18 字，强结论/强利益点）
  - 小字补充（20-40 字，限定人群/场景/边界）
  - 版式建议（居中/左对齐）、配色建议（高对比易读）
  - 背景风格（纯色/渐变/轻纹理），避免信息噪音

### 6) 发布（在获得用户明确授权后）

原则：默认只提供“怎么做”的步骤与准备清单；只有在用户明确授权后，才执行账号内动作，并回传每一步结果。

#### 6.1 授权与前置检查

- 明确要执行的动作：发帖（文字配图）
- 若用户未登录或当前不可操作：改为输出“手动操作步骤 + 检查点”，不要臆造已执行结果

#### 6.2 发帖（文字配图）

- 发布前检查：
  - 标题、正文、标签、地点（如适用）齐全
  - 合规限制已满足（避免敏感词/极限词/医疗化表述等）
  - 已在“文字配图”模块生成大字图（无需上传本地图片/视频）
- 输入顺序与字段分离（防止 # 混入正文导致输入错误）：
  - 先把标题输入到标题栏（只放标题，不含任何 # 标签）
  - 再把正文输入到正文栏（正文里不要写 # 话题标签）
  - 最后在标签/话题入口单独添加 3-8 个标签（每个标签单独添加；不要把 #tag 作为正文的一部分粘贴）
- 发布步骤（按平台 UI 顺序）：
  - 进入发帖 → 选择“文字配图” → 生成大字图 → 填标题 → 填正文 → 单独添加标签/话题与地点 → 预览检查 → 发布
- 发布后回传：
  - 发布状态（成功/失败/需手动）与原因
  - 发布链接（如可获得）
  - 建议的首小时互动策略（例如：置顶评论/引导提问）

## 场景模板

### 评测类（3C/美妆）发布模板

- 标题：结论 + 对比对象 + 场景（通勤/学生党/敏感肌/油皮）
- 正文结构：购买结论 → 为什么（3 点）→ 对比（表格/要点）→ 适合/不适合 → 清单/避坑
- 视觉结构：对比图/细节图/场景图/参数或使用步骤图

### 旅游攻略发布模板

- 标题：城市/路线 + 天数 + 亮点（不踩雷/省钱/亲子友好）
- 正文结构：行程总览 → 每天路线 → 交通与时间 → 预算与住宿 → 必吃必去 → 避坑
- 视觉结构：路线图/地标图/菜单价格/排队时间/机位提示

# vc +meeting-list-active

列出当前进行中的会议，用来发现 `+meeting-events` 需要的长数字 `meeting_id`。

本 skill 对应 shortcut：`lark-cli vc +meeting-list-active`（调用 `GET /open-apis/vc/v1/bots/user_active_meeting`）。

## 命令

```bash
# 查询当前登录用户正在参加的会议
lark-cli vc +meeting-list-active --format json
```

## 返回范围

只返回当前登录用户正在参加的会议；返回空不代表当前用户没有在开会，只能说明没有找到该接口可发现的进行中会议。

## 多会议选择

- 如果返回多个会议，不要自动挑第一个。
- 向用户展示每个候选的 `meeting_title` / `meeting_no` / `meeting_id`，等待用户选择。
- 选择后执行 `+meeting-events` 读取事件。

## 9 位会议号匹配

用户提供 9 位会议号时，把会议号当作 active meeting 的筛选条件，而不是写操作指令。

匹配规则：

- 在返回会议中匹配 `meeting_no == <9位会议号>`。
- 匹配到唯一会议：取该项的长数字 `meeting_id`，后续调用 `+meeting-events`。
- 匹配到多个会议：展示候选，让用户选择。
- 没有匹配：说明当前登录用户没有发现该会议号对应的 active meeting。

## 常见错误与排查

| 错误现象 | 根本原因 | 解决方案 |
|---------|---------|---------|
| 返回空列表 | 当前登录用户没有可见的进行中会议 | 确认用户是否在会中，或是否切错 profile |
| 无权限 / 不可见 | 当前登录用户没有可见的进行中会议，或凭证异常 | 确认用户是否在会中、是否切错 profile；若凭证缺失由 agent 平台补齐用户凭证后重试 |

# 双节经营方法

## 认知来源与使用方法

本节是 Skill 内置的双节历史定性方法，由开发阶段提供的「重点方向」「价格带」「商品类型」「商品关键词／高销品画像」「双节餐饮大盘洞察」资料归纳而成。原始资料包含自助餐等细分餐饮样本，不能直接外推到全部餐饮，更不能作为酒旅、休娱等行业的统一价格、增速或客群结论。运行报告引用本节时，来源写“Skill 内置历史定性方法”，不得写成当次用户提供资料或平台实时数据。

使用稳定的节日认知指导判断：中秋通常围绕团圆、亲子与本地家庭；国庆可围绕出游、朋友相聚、地方特色与本地休闲。哪类客群对当前门店重要，仍由本店位置、商品与实际人群信息判断。国庆不意味着每座城市或每家店都由游客驱动。

历史资料用于定性解释，不要求每次实时更新行业大盘，也不引用旧图中的具体涨幅、爆发日期、城市占比作为今年预测。当前搜索、热点与同行样例另取真实数据；不能把参考词库称作当前高搜榜。

## 11 个经营维度

| 维度 | 需要识别的双节差异 | 对应诊断与动作 |
|---|---|---|
| 消费人数 | 中秋家庭、三代同行；国庆双人出游、朋友及家庭小团体；日常单人需求仍存在 | 检查单人、双人、家庭和多人选择是否匹配；补齐缺口或保留主力，不一律加大套餐 |
| 食材 | 餐饮可突出秋季时令、地方特色、招牌或真实高价值食材 | 从现有供应提炼卖点；适合才建议上新。大闸蟹、羊肉、桂花等仅是候选，不强加到不相关品类 |
| 节日含义 | 中秋强调团圆与陪伴；国庆强调相聚、出游与休闲体验 | 转成商品场景、体验或文案，不只加节日前缀 |
| 抖音短视频运营 | 节前需要让顾客知道卖什么、适合谁；节中更需要到店路线、实际体验、时段和可用信息 | 具体到选题、开头、画面、真实卖点、关联商品与发布时间；用同一组素材适配不同节点 |
| 消费场景 | 家庭聚餐、亲子陪伴、朋友聚会、途中便捷消费、地方尝鲜、周边游、本地休闲等 | 按门店实际位置和供给筛选场景，解释为什么适合该店 |
| 价格带 | 总价随人数、组合、房型或服务时长分层；节前计划型购买与节中即需购买不同 | 只用于理解客群与商品结构，不输出价格、折扣或涨降价调整建议 |
| 餐型 | 餐饮中双人餐可持续承担基础需求，四人／多人餐可承接节中聚餐 | 核对现有结构、份量与适用时段；餐型对非餐饮不适用，不硬贴标签 |
| 商品品类 | 团购套餐、适合的次卡／预售、家庭房、联票、多人场次、节日服务组合等 | 根据行业评估单品、组合、时段、有效期及售卖和核销安排 |
| 名字 | 节日场景要让用户快速识别人数与真实卖点 | 用“节日＋人数／场景＋真实卖点”组织；优先表达关键内容，不堆词，不承诺未提供的服务 |
| 消费趋势 | 对比平时与假期、节前购买与节中消费、本地与异地需求，但不预设确定涨幅 | 将历史方向与本店结构结合，区分已观察事实与需要验证的机会 |
| 运营活动 | 中秋团圆赠礼与亲子体验；国庆打卡、聚会、路线推荐；节前准备与节中履约 | 明确对象、权益、日期、参与条件、供给和观察指标；赠品及额外人力仅在必要时核对 |

以上维度用于内部诊断和建议标签，不是 11 条必出建议。维度标签需由建议内容支撑，不能只为覆盖数量贴上“食材”或“消费趋势”。

## 行业适配

| 行业 | 中秋可以考虑 | 国庆可以考虑 | 商品与履约要点 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 正餐、火锅、自助等 | 家庭团圆、三代同桌、适配亲子、真实时令食材 | 朋友聚会、家庭聚餐、游客尝鲜与地方招牌 | 人数、菜品和份量、价格梯度、儿童规则、可用日期、预约、大桌与出餐；自助“畅吃”仅在真实规则允许时使用 |
| 轻快餐、饮品、面包甜点 | 双人分享、家庭加餐、适合的团圆甜品或礼赠 | 途中便捷消费、随行分享、商圈即需、地方小吃 | 保留单人便捷供给；检查制作和取餐时段、携带便利；不要套四人正餐或高价值食材模型 |
| 酒店、民宿、旅游、景区 | 家庭陪伴、周边小住、亲子体验 | 多日出游、家庭旅行、双人同行、当地体验 | 入住／游玩日期、间夜／张数、房型及入住人数、儿童政策、早餐或附加服务、预约、假期可用与加价、库存。食材及餐型仅在真实餐饮服务涉及时适用 |
| 休闲娱乐、亲子游乐、运动体验 | 本地家庭与亲子陪伴、朋友小聚 | 多人社交、本地休闲、游客空闲时段 | 人数、场次、包间／项目、时长、预约、年龄限制、节假日加价和接待；“四人餐”映射为实际多人体验，不改变业务名称 |
| 丽人及其他到店服务 | 节前准备、陪伴同行、已存在的节日服务组合 | 出游前准备、假期休闲、错峰预约 | 项目内容、服务时长、技师／设备时段、预约与真实权益；不强行设置聚餐、食材和多人套餐 |

没有证据的行业方向表述为候选机会，不能写“本店家庭客群占主导”等未经核验的事实。

## 商品诊断顺序

1. **能否用**：目标店、售卖状态、有效期、假期限制、日期、预约、加价与容量。
2. **是否适合**：人数／房型／服务单元、内容、份量、场景与不同客群。
3. **是否看得懂**：名称、主图、完整内容、实际计价单位与使用说明。
4. **价值是否清楚**：价格梯度、招牌／特色、已有服务和真实权益。
5. **能否被找到和承接**：搜索词、短视频选题、商品关联和活动入口。

同一问题合并成一个动作。例如，四人餐节假日不可用，应先处理规则，再把推广排在规则确认之后；不能一边指出不可用，一边建议立即放量宣传。

## 内容、同行与投流

- 内容方向先匹配品类、场景和真实商品，再看热度。每个方向写出商家能拍的具体画面与卖点，不只列话题词。
- 区分真实热点、商户搜索需求、历史关键词和创意建议。热点与活动以实际时间及有效期判断，不将固定“72 小时”套给所有话题，也不引入无关的下季度前瞻。
- 同行只学习可见的组合、命名、内容或规则；没有成交及归因证据，不能说“竞品靠这个活动增长了多少”。
- 投流有记录：比较同口径的素材、商品和场景，提出延续或改测方向；转化问题来自商品不可用时先修商品。无投流：给内容和商品准备建议，不虚构复盘。只使用本次分析范围与当前窗口的记录；近 30 日零消耗不推断全部历史未投放。
- 不默认给预算档位或精确分配比例。确实需要增加预算、设限量或提供赠品时，核对最少必要成本与容量；无法核实时，提出条件性建议并把未确定部分隔离清楚。

## 节奏安排

- 节前：核对商品可用性及组合，完成名称与内容准备，按适配情况预售或预约。
- 中秋：以已确认的团圆、亲子或陪伴场景执行，观察预约、成交、核销与体验反馈。
- 两节之间（如有）：复盘已发生表现，调整内容表达、库存和预约说明，切换国庆场景；生成报告时未发生的数据不能预填成复盘结论。
- 国庆：按本店实际客群承接出游、聚会或本地休闲，保障可用供给，结合容量控制推广。

日期相邻、重合或仅剩一个节日未到时，依据目标年份和当前阶段调整。不以历史截图的冲锋日替代本年的日历。

# 设计系统总纲与场景路由

**这是"选定设计系统"这一步的入口。** 一份演示文稿只选一套设计系统，它统一决定这份 deck 的配色、字体、留白、版式等所有视觉决策。

使用方式（三步）：

1. **遵守通用规则**：本文「通用规则」适用于全部七个场景的所有页面，与所选场景的风格文档一起生效，但用户指定的模板、排版、品牌规范、配色、字体、参考风格优先于本指南。
2. **判定场景**：根据用户输入选择唯一匹配的主场景。
3. **读取场景文档**：读取该场景对应的风格文档，按其表达重点与方法进行设计。

> **卡片用法的唯一裁决者是设计系统本身，其它任何文档都不得再追加"要不要用卡片"的规则。**
> - 匹配到七个场景之一 → **禁止**用任何卡片，用线条、留白、字号对比替代。
> - 不匹配任何场景 → 回退到兜底设计系统 [`fallback.md`](fallback.md)
> - 用户直接给了模板/品牌规范/配色/字体/参考风格等其他要求 → 以用户为准。

## 第一步：通用规则

> 以下通用规则约束「匹配到具体场景」时的设计。回退到兜底 [`fallback.md`](fallback.md) 时，以兜底文档为准。

### 要求

1. **每页都有明确的读者任务**：这一页要让读者理解什么、相信什么、决定什么或做什么——动手设计前先想清楚。
2. **翻页有节奏**：自行判断是否需要目录页或章节页；读者翻阅时应能感到节奏变化——有的页面一眼看完，有的值得停下细读。
3. **灵活使用图表与形状组合**：当一段信息可以用超出当前图表语法表达能力的复杂图示来呈现时，鼓励灵活用形状等手段构建这种表达，但是shape使用不得出现在封面页、结尾页和章节分割页。
5. **合理使用搜图/生图**：用搜图/生图工具获取图片并放到合适位置。但严禁滥用图片。用户上传的附件里若有可用图片，用在合适的页面上，如果不是用户指定不能用搜图结果放在封面上，封面只支持高质量图。
6. **以用户和主题为准**：用户指定的模板、品牌规范、配色、字体、参考风格和要使用的附件优先于本指南。
7. **来源标注**：涉及外部事实和数据的页面必须标明来源、日期或时间区间、以及口径。来源文本用 `<a href="url">` 超链接指向原始报告或数据页；脚注里引用具体来源时同样用 `<a href="url">` 链接到原始出处，强化专业可信度。
8. **排版均衡分割**：同一层级且同一行横向并列的多卡片/模块/栏目，默认必须采用 等宽均分 布局，保证视觉重心平衡，不允许出现肉眼明显不均的宽度分配。同层级模块的 对齐基线 需统一，包括顶部对齐、底部对齐或内容起始位置对齐。只有在需要通过版面宽度表达内容主次关系时，才允许非等宽布局。
9. **结构化信息必须使用原生表格**：涉及数据对比、指标清单、参数说明、维度拆解、结构化信息呈现时，必须使用 Slides 原生 `<table>` 或合适的图表组件承载，不得在页面文案或 XML 中输出 Markdown 表格（如 `| 字段 | 数值 |`）。Markdown 表格只适合说明文档，不是幻灯片可渲染的结构化组件。
10. **图表专业度**：扇形图、环形图需要保障每一个图例颜色有足够视觉区分度，不能出现一样的颜色，可以用主色组合其他颜色，这是全slides内唯一允许使用主题色和辅助色以外颜色的地方，也可使用slides内主题色不同透明度梯度进行区分。
11. **保障信息区分度** 序号和文字如果字号相同且平行的话之间需要有一个空格；前置小标题（含加粗文字）与后续阐释内容之间需有明确间隔，可通过空格、中文冒号或换行实现。
12. **目录是决定质量的关键**：目录页必须避免“小字堆叠”和“大面积空白”两种问题，章节模块需要均匀铺满页面；若单列排布无法保证舒展和均衡，应自动改为左右双列布局。可以用大字和小字组合，一个章节标题下面辅以小字号说明。章节编号与章节名称不要放在一个文本框内挤在一起。
13. **用户机构配色是配色参考优先级最高的**：如果用户说明了具体的所属比如学校、公司、机构等，需要先执行搜索对应的logo，用对应主色制作ppt要好于用style推荐。
14. **符号使用规范**：必须严格区分全角与半角符号中文语境下统一使用全角中文标点，英文单词、数字、代码、URL、文件路径及技术标识中统一使用半角符号；不得混用或误用，确保表达专业、版式统一、可读性稳定。


### 严格禁止

- **证据边界**：不得编造数据、引用、客户案例、实验结果或来源；素材缺失时，明确标注为占位、假设或待补充信息。
- **经典 AI 套路**：非用户要求严禁用卡片搭建层级或对齐（圆角矩形、矩形卡片、带色条的卡片）——线条、留白和字号对比是更好的方案；严禁把红、紫、黄、绿一股脑堆在同一页的 AI 配色。
- **禁止彩虹色和靠色**：如果不是skill指定参考配色，禁止用大于三种颜色在一个slides内。禁止文字和背景靠色，必须谨慎保障文字能够清晰展示不溶于背景。
- **query里的明亮不代表彩虹**：要求明亮也只能使用三种以内颜色，要合理搭配
- **禁止堆叠目录**：目录页必须避免“小字堆叠”和“大面积空白”两种问题，章节模块需要均匀铺满页面；若单列排布无法保证舒展和均衡，应自动改为左右双列布局。章节编号与章节名称不要放在一个文本框内挤在一起。
- **禁止滥用shape**：禁止在章节页和封面用抽象shape，用高质量图片是更好的选择
- **禁止滥用截图**：如果图片来自于用户附件，图片必须原汁原味使用，不得进行图片切割，应该让排版适应图片而不是图片适应排版。

### 用户上传了 PPTX 模板的用法

**用户上传 PPTX 附件要求"参考"其风格或者用这个模板做ppt时并不是把它当整套模板逐页复用，一旦附件内有pptx并且用户意图是用这个pptx作为模板做ppt时先按以下方法处理后再路由对应的style参考设计原则**：

1. **先看渲染效果，别止步于抠文字**：实际打开样本，截图看清页面真实呈现的视觉效果；只跑xml提取拿到一堆文字不算看懂模板。
2. **提炼一份精简的参考要点，不逐页照搬**，按三类记录可迁移的东西：
  - **可迁移的版式手法**：如模板的网格骨架、配色规则、步骤式导航、证据分区等结构性设计。
  - **可迁移的风格**：如克制、亲和、严谨，或活动现场感、公务通传感等基调倾向。
  - **可迁移的图形语法**：如并列模块、时间轴路径、嵌套层级、取景框等表达手法。
3. **不能修改的东西**：主要字体、背景图片（尺寸跟ppt一样大的视为背景）、模板自带的品牌标识、真实人物/照片、原始文案、专属色值、装饰纹样——这些必须在新设计内保留，但是可以灵活的进行设计。
4. **设计时对应页面类型**：判断内容表达更适配里的哪一类，不要把这点局部经验放大成整套页面的通用规则。
5. 没有合适的可以直接使用的页面时按照合适的设计系统自行搭建。


## 第二步：判定场景

根据用户输入，分析演示文稿的受众和读者任务，判定它所属的场景，并读取对应的风格文档。

> 选择一个主场景。确有必要时可以再加一个辅助场景，但必须以主场景为准。

| 场景类型 | 典型诉求 | 读者任务 | 风格文档 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 分析决策 | 咨询、金融、行业研究、战略、市场机会、商业分析、投资分析 | 比较选项、形成判断、支撑决策 | [`strategy-and-analysis.md`](strategy-and-analysis.md) |
| 商业提案 | 营销方案、销售提案、融资路演、招商/招投资、产品提案、商业计划书 | 理解价值、相信方案、采取行动 | [`business-pitch.md`](business-pitch.md) |
| 管理汇报 | 工作汇报、项目复盘、季度总结、OKR、管理简报、职业培训 | 掌握现状、暴露问题、确认行动 | [`business-review.md`](business-review.md) |
| 学术研究 | 研究生课题、论文答辩、科研项目、开题报告、中期报告、结题/汇报 | 评估问题、方法、证据与贡献 | [`academic-research.md`](academic-research.md) |
| 教育培训 / 知识科普 | K12 课件、教学演示、患者教育、专业科普 | 理解、记住、正确应用或行动 | [`learning-and-training.md`](learning-and-training.md) |
| 技术工程 | 工程方案、架构评审、研发报告、AI / 数据 / 运维 / 安全 | 看清结构、依赖、指标与取舍 | [`technical-presentation.md`](technical-presentation.md) |
| 品牌 / 创意展示 | 品牌故事、设计提案、作品集、文化活动、人物介绍、影片艺术品介绍 | 建立认知、留下记忆、形成认同 | [`brand-storytelling.md`](brand-storytelling.md) |

**兜底**：如果演示文稿明显不属于以上任何场景，不要强行套最接近的一个——回退到兜底设计系统 [`fallback.md`](fallback.md)（信息密度极高的图文卡片布局）。

## 字体系统

除用户明确要求繁体中文、港澳台语境或原文素材本身为繁体外，中文内容默认使用简体中文；不要为营造风格感轻易改写成繁体字，避免字体缺字、fallback 字体不一致或跨端渲染异常。

| 字体名称 | 语种 | 字体类型 | 风格与特点 | 适用场景 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 思源黑体 | 中文 | 无衬线（黑体） | 结构规整，屏幕可读性最稳 | 通用、汇报、技术 |
| 思源宋体 | 中文 | 衬线（宋体） | 笔画有对比，端正典雅 | 学术、文化、正式演示 |
| 寒蝉锦书宋 | 中文 | 衬线（细宋） | 纤细修长，书卷气浓 | 文化、品牌、艺术 |
| 寒蝉团圆体 圆体 | 中文 | 圆体 | 圆头笔画饱满，活泼亲和 | 儿童、生活方式、娱乐 |
| 霞鹜 975 圆体 | 中文 | 圆体 | 圆润柔和，克制耐看 | 教育、科普、生活方式 |
| 有字库龙藏体 | 中文 | 书法（毛笔） | 毛笔行楷，笔锋凌厉 | 国风、文化、海报 |
| 楷体 | 中文 | 系统楷书 | 结构端正，免安装 | 传统文化、引文 |
| Inter | 拉丁 | 无衬线 | 屏幕优先，小字号清晰 | 通用、数据密集页 |
| IBM Plex Sans | 拉丁 | 无衬线（工程感） | 机械与人文混合 | 技术、工程、研究 |
| Nunito | 拉丁 | 无衬线（圆角） | 圆角终端，亲和友好 | 教育、科普、消费 |
| Montserrat | 拉丁 | 无衬线（几何） | 招牌风格，大写气场强 | 提案、营销、封面 |
| Josefin Sans | 拉丁 | 无衬线（Art Deco） | 复古装饰风，字面偏小 | 创意、文化 |
| Bebas Neue | 拉丁 | 窄体全大写 | 仅大写，冲击力克制 | 海报、封面 |
| Anton | 拉丁 | 超粗窄体 | 视觉重量最大 | 口号、关键数据、巨字页 |
| Barlow Condensed | 拉丁 | 窄体无衬线 | 微方轮廓，字重齐全 | 技术、工业、数据页 |
| EB Garamond | 拉丁 | 衬线（古典） | 人文气质，长文舒适 | 学术、人文 |
| Lora | 拉丁 | 衬线（书卷） | 笔刷式曲线，书卷气 | 研究、品牌叙事 |
| Merriweather | 拉丁 | 衬线（屏幕优化） | 字形结实，小字号清晰 | 报告、教育 |
| Playfair Display | 拉丁 | 衬线（高对比） | 对比强烈，杂志感 | 品牌、时尚、封面 |
| Roboto Mono | 拉丁 | 等宽 | 中性等宽，数字对齐 | 指标、表格、代码 |
| 源ノ角ゴシック | 日文 | 黑体 | 思源黑体日文版 | 日文页面 |
| 본고딕 | 韩文 | 黑体 | 思源黑体韩文版 | 韩文页面 |
| Times New Roman | 拉丁 | 衬线 | 正式文档默认字体 | 公文、投稿硬性要求 |


## 图表选型通用规则
- **大原则是：除非具体的 style 文档有提及优先级，否则优先用原生图表、然后是 shape 组合，最后是 svg 图表**

### 四类工具的分工

1. **原生 `<chart>`** — 柱 / 条 / 折线 / 阶梯 / 面积 / 饼 / 雷达 / 组合。必须先用 [`../../scripts/slides_chart_tool.py`](../../scripts/slides_chart_tool.py) 获取对应 XML 片段，再照抄工具输出;视觉规格以所选场景文档为准。**优点:数据和样式都是 Slides 对象可直接编辑。** 这是绝大多数商业/通用场景的默认。原生图表截图检查时，如果发现有一些问题存在的话，应该尝试进行优化，而不是简单的切换成 shape 或 svg 类型。

2. **SVG 图表库** — `chart_help()` 提供简明条件与名称索引，`chart_help('<slug>')` 查签名；`chart_slide(slug, x=, y=, width=, height=, **kwargs)` 按框尺寸出图并返回半可编辑片段（文字原生、同色色块可整体换色）。适用于有数据支撑的专业表达；改内容要回去改 kwargs 重跑。普通趋势不能换成归因，均值 ± SEM 不能换成效应量 + CI。

3. **SVG 关系库** — 树 / 层级 / 分类 / 鱼骨 / 流程 / 组织架构。`relation_help(...)` 看 slug;正式 Slides 必须用 `make_relation_atomized(..., strict_no_embed=True)` 或 CLI `--atomized` 输出可编辑元素,**树状图主体不得用 `<embed>`**。

4. **drawing 库 / 手写 SVG + atomize** — 原生 chart 做不到也不属于关系库的自定义示意图 / 概念图 / 装饰图形。规则见 [`../xml/svg-writing-guide.md`](../xml/svg-writing-guide.md)。
